ca_lake_arrowhead_pinnacles.blurb: A cluster of small granite peaks northwest of Lake Arrowhead in the San Bernardino Mountains. Thick chaparral and manzanita blanket the slopes, and use-trails fork off in every direction, so some of the farther walls take real effort to reach. Sport and trad split the climbing almost evenly, with a few top-rope lines. Most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with the 5.10s the largest group, a modest number of 5.12s and a few easy lines at the bottom. Local climbers often liken the quality of the stone to Joshua Tree. Main Ridge Pinnacles, Rotten Rock Valley, Shooting Gallery and Main Meadow hold the most climbs. A smaller eastern group nearby offers cracks and face climbs well off the beaten path.

ar_east_side.blurb: The long west-facing cliff line along the eastern edge of the canyon at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, in north-central Arkansas just west of Jasper. The climbing is on sandstone. Sport routes are the bulk, backed by a solid group of trad lines and a good number of boulder problems. Routes run from about 5.6 to 5.12, centred on the 5.8 to 5.11 range, and the boulders span V0 to V12 with plenty in the low and middle grades. The routes here tend to be longer than average, and the bouldering is spread out rather than clustered. It is split into many sectors, led by Middle East, Far East, Land of the Lost and Roman Wall.

ca_scheelite_canyon_pratt_s_crack_gully.blurb: A side canyon within Pine Creek Canyon, above Bishop on the Eastern Sierra side. Pine Creek itself is a granite canyon lying between Mount Tom and the Wheeler Crest, with views across the Owens Valley. This gully packs in a dense run of walls, including Mustache Wall, Planetarium and Gecko Wall, Oser Wall and Ministry Wall. Sport routes outnumber trad by roughly two to one. The difficulty leans hard: most lines are 5.11 and 5.12, with a fair spread of 5.10s, a handful of 5.13s and only a few easier routes. Across the canyon, climbing is best from late spring to late fall, many routes sit in shade, and summer mornings and evenings are often pleasant.

ca_west_shore.blurb: Lake Tahoe's western shoreline, where the climbing runs from roadside boulders up to ridgetop cliffs near the Sierra crest. Its main zones surround Emerald Bay: Eagle Creek Canyon, with small granite crags holding sport, trad, top-rope routes and winter ice, and the boulders at D.L. Bliss State Park. Cascade Cliff adds more sport. The mix is varied, with trad, bouldering and sport in similar numbers plus a few alpine lines. Rock climbs mostly sit in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with some 5.13 and a scattering of easier routes, while problems run from V0 through the V7 and V8 range. Fall is traditionally the best time around Tahoe, though climbing is possible all year when the rock is dry.

ca_barker_dam_area.blurb: A scatter of separate rock formations in central Joshua Tree National Park, set in Mojave Desert terrain of monzogranite boulders, Joshua trees and sandy washes. Climbing is split across many formations rather than one big cliff. Trad leads, followed by bouldering and top-rope, with only a small amount of sport. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.11, with the 5.10s the biggest group, while boulder problems are mostly easy to moderate. Black Rocks, Gunsmoke Area, Indian Wave Boulders and Hunk Rock are the biggest pieces. Bouldering is best in fall, winter and spring; summer heat can pass 100 degrees with little shade.

co_old_stage_road.blurb: A long dirt road leaving western Colorado Springs for Cripple Creek along the southern flanks of Pikes Peak, with climbing at crags dotted along the way. Rock quality swings from mediocre to superb, and the feel is adventurous even at the developed crags: steep bushwhacking approaches and thin beta are common. Trad is the main game, with a solid helping of sport and a little bouldering. Grades run from about 5.4 to 5.13, with the bulk of routes in the 5.7 to 5.11 range and 5.10 the most common. The Gallery, Cathedral Park, The Citadel and School of Rock hold the most climbs. Sunny winter days of about 30 degrees or warmer can still be climbable.
